subject: Urgent: SummitWorks renewal strategy & capacity uplift
messages:
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@summitworks.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Li <evan.li@summitworks.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal, capacity needs, and a new vendor at the table

Monica,

Thanks for the check-in earlier this week. We are approaching our platform renewal (contract end 2026-12-31) and I wanted to flag two things on our side:

1) Usage growth: Q4 forecasts now show a potential 60% increase in peak concurrent tokens due to a planned personalization rollout. We need guidance on whether our current Dedicated pool can scale to meet that without re-architecting.

2) Competitive pressure: Our infra team ran a short benchmark with Altai AI; they surfaced a managed offer that promises similar latency at ~20% lower unit cost if we commit 12 months. They also propose a migration assistance package.

We value the stability Redwood has provided, but the procurement team is asking for a concrete upsell/price-capacity proposal and a short remediation plan if performance gaps appear. Can you put together an operational playbook and a delta-cost model this week? Evan is looping procurement on next steps.

—Alyssa
Director, Platform Engineering
SummitWorks Inc

Attachments: none
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@summitworks.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal, capacity needs, and a new vendor at the table

Alyssa — thank you for the heads up and for sharing the context. High level response below; we'll follow with a short playbook doc and cost scenarios by Thursday EOD.

- Capacity: you can scale your Dedicated pool to handle +60% peak with a targeted uplift and autoscale policy; no app rewrite needed in most cases. We will propose a pre-warm/burst configuration to avoid cold-start latency for peak windows.
- Benchmark comparatives: we will run a 48h side-by-side with your representative workload (same prompts, sequence lengths, and concurrency) — Redwood will cover the testing fees.
- Commercial: we can present a capacity + term bundle with a scoped discount if you commit to a 12-month uplift and a 30% reserved commit.

Dev and Laura — can you own a short ops playbook (runbook for pre-warm, caching settings, and rollback policy) and a cost model that compares: current committed spend, 12-month uplift w/ reserved commit, and Altai-style managed alternative? Alyssa — want to schedule a 30-min call after we run the tests; what times work for you Thursday?

Thanks,
Monica
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Folks — taking the lead on the technical side. Initial plan:

1) Test harness: Laura and I will deploy a synthetic load mirroring SummitWorks' anonymized prompt set. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, token cost, and KV-cache hit rates.
2) Pre-warm approach: propose a short-lived warmed pool timed to expected peaks with predictive scaling based on their telemetry (we'll outline required metrics and a webhook).
3) Fallbacks: recommend a read-only fallback variant (size-reduced model) for non-critical requests to preserve SLAs during overload.
4) Timeline: 48h benchmark starting Thu 18:00 PST; deliverables: benchmark PDF and cost_model_scenarios.xlsx by Sat 12:00 PST.

Laura — please include a short ops-runbook (1-2 pages) that the SummitWorks SREs can follow.

—Dev

Thanks — Thursday works. We can provide a 24h anonymized production trace for the benchmark. Two asks for the bakeoff:

- Can Redwood demonstrate the pre-warm plan without impacting our live traffic? We need to know rollback steps explicitly.
- Procurement is sensitive to termination clauses and migration assistance in case we decide to switch. Please include a migration-runbook or at least an exportable KV snapshot procedure.

Also, Ben from Altai reached out to outline their offer; I'm attaching their proposal so you can see their scope and pricing. Procurement will be on the call.

Alyssa

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@summitworks.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Nov 2026 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: SummitWorks benchmark & recommended operational playbook (draft)

Alyssa — attaching the draft benchmark report and the ops playbook highlights below. Full PDFs delivered via Drive link. Quick summary:

- Benchmark results (48h synthetic): Redwood default model configs matched Altai p50 latency within 5% and outperformed p95 by ~8% on the same GPU family. Token-unit cost under our default burst settings was ~12% lower than Altai's listed managed rate in their proposal.

- Key operational recommendations:
  * Pre-warm pool sized to +75% of your current peak with a 15-minute warm window before business-critical events.
  * KV/Prefix caching: enable prefix cache for common personalization prompts — expected 22% reduction in token throughput during peak.
  * Autoscale: predictive autoscaler with a 1.5x headroom setting and an emergency burst lane on Dedicated.
  * Rollback: immediate traffic split back to steady-state (pre-warm off) + auto-fail to a smaller quantized model if p95 > SLO for >120s.

- Migration/export: we provide a validated KV snapshot procedure and an export of model artifacts consistent with industry standard checkpoints; full doc attached.

Commercial notes (Rishi copied): to achieve price parity with Altai's 12-month managed offer, we can structure a 12-month uplift with a 25% reserved commit and a performance credit schedule for missed p95 targets. The credit schedule is contingent on observed traffic shape.

Deliverables: summit_benchmark_report.pdf, cost_model_scenarios.xlsx, ops_runbook.pdf (links below).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SummitWorksRenewal
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/DEAL-SW-2026-11
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/contract/ABC-123-SW-Renewal

Laura Bennett

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: procurement@summitworks.com, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Final proposal: renewal term + capacity uplift (next steps)

Alyssa / Evan / procurement team — thanks for the collaborative test. Based on the benchmark and ops runbook, here is Redwood's final commercial proposal and recommended next steps:

1) Offer: 12-month term with a 25% reserved-capacity commit on your Dedicated pool, plus a 60% temporary uplift during Q1 launch windows.
2) Pricing: blended unit rate that yields ~15% cost advantage vs Altai's published managed rate when the 25% commit is accepted. Detailed numbers are in cost_model_scenarios.xlsx.
3) SLA & credits: formal p95 latency SLO with stepwise credits for missed targets (details in DocuSign).
4) Migration protection: export/runbook included and one week of white-glove migration assistance if you elect to terminate within the first 90 days — ensures data portability.

Next steps:
- Procurement: confirm final legal terms and accept or send redlines within 5 business days.
- Technical: Laura/Dev to schedule an on-call run for pre-warm activation during your launch window.
- Commercial: Monica to prepare an executive summary and a short one-pager for your CFO.

We believe this structure balances performance, cost, and operational safety. Let us know if you want a 1:1 with Rishi and Monica to walk the finance team through the numbers.

—Rishi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: cost_model_scenarios.xlsx, summit_benchmark_report.pdf
